ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The image shows a fused bicyclic structure: a benzene ring fused to a partially unsaturated nitrogen-containing ring. The ring nitrogen is bonded to an acyl group drawn as R-C(=O)-, and the right-hand ring carbon bears a substituent leading to a protonated terminal nitrogen fragment. Curved arrows are drawn in the image, but the question says to ignore them. Reasoning: Following the assigned transcription method, replace the left R substituent with * to give the acyl fragment *C(=O). Attach that carbonyl carbon to the ring nitrogen, giving *C(=O)N1. From that N, traverse through the fused benzene as c2ccccc2, then continue around the partially unsaturated heterocycle as C=CC1 to close back to the original N. Finally append the right-hand substituent as C#[NH+]. Combining these parts gives *C(=O)N1c2ccccc2C=CC1C#[NH+].
